facts.statement: The only known fossils of Cathartornis gracilis consist of two tarsometatarsi, one complete and one partial.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Cathartornis gracilis, known from only two tarsometatarsi, one complete and the other represented by its distal end.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cathartornis were found in Late Pleistocene deposits at the La Brea Tar Pits in Southern California.
facts.quote: Both specimens were recovered from the Late Pleistocene deposits of the La Brea Tar Pits in Southern California.

facts.statement: No additional fossils have been assigned to Cathartornis, though some remains previously classified as Teratornis might belong to this genus.
facts.quote: To date, no additional fossils have been referred to Cathartornis, although some remains currently assigned to Teratornis may represent the former.

facts.statement: Cathartornis is an extinct genus of bird belonging to the family Teratornithidae.
facts.quote: Cathartornis ("Cathartes Bird") is an extinct taxon of bird of the family Teratornithidae.

facts.statement: Unpublished fossil material has been mentioned in connection with the genus Cathartornis.
facts.quote: Unpublished fossil material has also been mentioned in connection with the genus.

facts.statement: Cathartornis lived during the Late Pleistocene, between 0.129 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Late Pleistocene (0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago)
